newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends down on faded HK rally hope.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends down on faded HK rally hope.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended down on Wednesday with institutions offsetting their positions mainly in real estate Pudong shares as hopes of a rally before the Hong Kong handover finally faded, brokers said.
The B share index fell 1.487 points or 1.75 percent to 83.457 on volume of 14.195 million shares worth $8.461 million.

Pudong shares saw a correction today on institutional profit-taking due to uncertainties about the government's attitude toward the market after the handover of Hong Kong at midnight on June 30, brokers said.
"Heavy institutional selling in Pudong shares pushed the index down," said one broker.
"With the approach of the Hongkong handover, institutions cannot find any new excuse to boost buying interest, and have begun to liquidate their positions," another broker said.

Shanghai shares surged earlier this year on expectations that Beijing would want the stock markets to boom through the handover, but the meteoric rise caused government regulators to step in in May and brought prices down.
Of 44 shares, 41 traded, with 27 down, 10 flat and four up.
Shanghai Dazhong Taxi was the biggest loser on institutional profit-taking, slipping $0.046 or 4.97 percent to $0.878 on volume of 1.0 million shares.
Pudong shares Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development also fell sharply on institutional selling to unwind positions, down $0.036 or 4.12 percent to $0.836 on volume of 896,000 shares.
Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle 900946.SS was the most actively traded on institutional profit-taking, shedding $0.026 or 4.86 percent to $0.508 on volume 4.0 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index consolidated on an uncertain market direction, brokers said.
The index dipped 6.147 points or 0.45 percent to 1,356.720 points on volume of 420.4 million shares worth 6.1 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index ended down 16.980 points or 0.41 percent to 4,136.621 points.
Huanghe Machinery and Electronics was the biggest loser on its poor prospects, tumbling 0.32 yuan or 5.57 percent to 5.42 yuan on volume of 1.4 million shares.
